title: NCERT Grade 11 Physics | Image | Page 9
text:
[IMAGE] This image illustrates the concept of measuring the **coefficient of viscosity** using a **viscometer** or by demonstrating viscous drag on a falling object, specifically through a setup involving a cylindrical rod or a simple fall through a viscous fluid.

The image appears to depict a method where a rod is being lowered through a viscous liquid (not shown but implied), and the hands are likely indicating the measurement of the **time taken for the rod to fall** or the **force required to move it at a constant speed**. This setup helps in understanding how viscous forces oppose the motion of an object through a fluid, which is crucial for studying fluid dynamics and viscosity. The concept is often linked to Stokes' Law, which relates the frictional force on spherical objects falling through a viscous fluid.
